note:
Ten floors of Ascendant devotion that rendered as a three-box stack on the shared asc_shrine arm. Built as a ZIGGURAT: seven square boxes stepping in from the podium to a tenth of its width, with a faceted drum lantern on the apex — the one silhouette in Coldwater that narrows the whole way and ends in a point rather than a lid. ⚠ NO AUTHORED `neon`, deliberately. `derivedStyle` reads `m.neon` as a TRUTH TEST for works-vs-front-vs-block, so authoring a colour here would reclassify a stone shrine as a SHOPFRONT and hang a retail kit on it; the accent it wants (#7fc8ff, off the stone family) is what `accentOf` already derives with the field left empty. RENDER_TUNE.legacyArms puts the asc_shrine arm back.

⚠ RESTORED TO THE HEIGHT OF ITS ARM (2026-09-17). The form above is unchanged and was
never the problem; what did not carry across from the asc_shrine arm was how tall it stands. It was
at 71% — 1.06x the storey stack against the arm's 1.50x — so every 'h'-tagged field
here was multiplied by 1.415 and every 'fh'-tagged one left alone. The silhouette is identical;
only the storeys are taller. Same regression as halcyontowers and thespire, same measurement.

⚠ AND THE UPLINK BEAM CAME BACK WITH THE HEIGHT. The asc_shrine arm ran a glowing Ascendant-blue
wire from the cap at 1.5 to 2.6 with a beacon on the end of it, and a server-rack glow on the
Curtain side — the whole reason the building reads as a shrine to a machine rather than as a
black ziggurat. None of it survived the port: this model emitted three sprites on a palette of
[20,28,44], which after dark is nothing at all. The beam is a helixRunner with r0 = r1 = 0 and
turns = 0, which is a straight vertical line through the same emitLightRunner the arm used.
